query: What pre-analysis plan and placebo-window conventions are standard and robust for event-study/DiD/synthetic-control designs detecting packaging-change effects?

response.query: What pre-analysis plan and placebo-window conventions are standard and robust for event-study/DiD/synthetic-control designs detecting packaging-change effects?
response.answer: For event-study/DiD/synthetic-control designs detecting packaging-change effects, a pre-analysis plan typically includes a clear timeline for pre- and post-treatment periods, while a placebo-window of similar length on either side of the treatment period is standard to control for timing effects.

results.title: Articles CONSORT-DEFINE explanation and elaboration ...
results.content: # Articles CONSORT-DEFINE explanation and elaboration: recommendations for enhancing reporting quality and impact of early phase dose-finding clinical trials. The international consensus-based CONSORT-DEFINE (Consolidated Standards for Reporting Trials Dose-finding Extension) statement, an extension of the CONSORT statement for randomised trials, was developed to improve the reporting of EPDF trials. For each new or modified checklist item, we provide a detailed description and its rationale with supporting evidence, and present examples from EPDF trial reports published in peer-reviewed scientific journals. When reporting the results of EPDF trials, authors are encouraged to consult the CONSORT-DEFINE E&E document, together with the CONSORT and CONSORT-DEFINE statement papers, and adhere to their recommendations. Widespread adoption of the CONSORT-DEFINE statement is likely to enhance the reporting quality of EPDF trials, thus facilitating the peer review of such studies and their appraisal by researchers, regulators, ethics committee members, and funders. This work is a further extension of the CONSORT-DEFINE study, which was funded by the UK Medical Research Council (MRC)-National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Methodology Research Programme (MR/T044934/1).
